rules.title: Just Cause Ordinance (JCO) – just cause required and relocation assistance for no-fault evictions
rules.requirement: Landlords of covered rental units in the City of Los Angeles may terminate a tenancy only for listed at-fault or no-fault just causes. For no-fault evictions, such as owner or family move-in, demolition or removal from the market, they must pay relocation assistance.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; relocation assistance for no-fault evictions
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.coverage_text: Most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the RSO, including buildings newer than October 1, 1978 and single-family dwellings. The tenant must have lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease must have expired, whichever comes first.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, cooperatives under certain circumstances, some non-profit homeless facilities or short-term substance abuse treatment centers, some HACLA or government-owned properties, and units subject to the RSO.
rules.interaction: The JCO covers units not regulated by the RSO. Single-family homes and condominiums exempt from state AB 1482 remain subject to the JCO.
rules.extraction_note: No ordinance number, enactment date or effective date given. The construction cutoff basis is described only as buildings 'newer than October 1, 1978'.

rules.title: Minimum arrears threshold for non-payment evictions (Fair Market Rent)
rules.requirement: Landlords of RSO and JCO units may not evict a tenant for falling behind in rent unless the amount owed exceeds the Fair Market Rent for the unit's bedroom size.
rules.key_value: Arrears must exceed one month's Fair Market Rent
rules.quoted_span: Effective March 27, 2023, landlords may not evict a tenant who falls behind in rent unless the tenant owes an amount higher than the Fair Market Rent (FMR).
rules.coverage_text: Applies to all RSO & JCO rental units.

rules.title: Eviction notices must be filed with LAHD
rules.requirement: Landlords must file every eviction notice served on a tenant in the City of Los Angeles with LAHD within three business days of service.
rules.key_value: File within 3 business days of service
rules.citation: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (JCO) / RSO
rules.quoted_span: All eviction notices issued to tenants in the City of Los Angeles must be filed with LAHD within three (3) business days of service on the tenant.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to all JCO & RSO rental properties.
rules.extraction_note: Effective date and source section not stated.

rules.title: AB 1482 California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 – annual rent cap
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases for covered units are limited to 5% plus the regional change in the cost of living, or 10%, whichever is lower. The page states the maximum was 8.9% for August 1, 2024 to July 31, 2025 in the Los Angeles region.
rules.quoted_span:
A
nual rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region in which the property is located, or 10% whichever is lower).
rules.coverage_text: Buildings older than 15 years, on a rolling basis.
rules.exemptions: Units built within the last 15 years (rolling); deed-restricted affordable units; certain dormitories; two-unit properties where the owner occupied the other unit for the entire tenancy; single-family homes and condos not owned by a REIT, corporation or LLC with a corporate member, where the tenant was given written notice of exemption; units subject to the LA RSO.
rules.interaction: Units already subject to the City of Los Angeles RSO are not covered by AB 1482. The JCO does not regulate rent increases.
rules.extraction_note: Described on a city webpage as background state law; enactment and effective dates are not stated. The construction cutoff is a rolling 15 years, not a fixed date. In the quoted span, the opening 'A' is split onto a separate line in the source and is reproduced verbatim with the line break.
